title: Reefer Cargo Services: Pre-Trip Inspection Charging and Validity
content:
Every container used under Reefer Cargo Services is inspected at the depot before it goes into service. When the allocated reefer passes, the service moves from requested to inspection passed and the inspection is charged. This page covers what is charged for an inspection, how long an inspection supports plugging the laden unit in at the load terminal, and what follows once that period has run out.

## Clause

Each inspection is charged. The inspection that brings the service to inspection passed is charged at the tier's inspection fee; any later inspection of the same service is charged at the tier's repeat inspection fee. An inspection supports plug-in for a limited period: its validity ends on the date of the most recent inspection charge on the service plus the tier's validity period, counted in calendar dates, and a plug-in taking place on that last day is still covered. A reefer that has not been plugged in by the end of that day is inspected again before it is plugged in, and that further inspection is charged at the repeat fee. An inspection charge can be booked only while the service stands at inspection passed. The dates are taken from the service's charge records, not from what the customer reports.

## Validity at a glance

| Plug-in date compared with the last covered day | Is the existing inspection enough for plug-in? |
|---|---|
| on or before the last covered day | yes |
| after the last covered day | no; a repeat inspection at the repeat fee is needed |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical figures)

Imagine a tier with a validity period of 10 calendar days, and a service whose most recent inspection was charged on 25 June 2026.

- The last covered day is 5 July 2026. A plug-in on 5 July is covered by that inspection.
- A plug-in on 6 July is not covered; the unit is inspected again and charged at the repeat fee.
- If the repeat inspection is charged on 7 July, it becomes the most recent inspection charge, and validity is then counted from 7 July.

## Points of judgement

- The count runs from the date the inspection was charged, not from the date the service was ordered.
- A repeat inspection does not cancel the charge of the earlier one; each inspection stands as its own charge.
- A service that has moved past inspection passed, for instance to plugged in, can no longer take an inspection charge.
